summary: One task of a round of the IO board component research (hardware/docs/Research.md)
logs: FU: 20 agents started (11 planned, 9 of 21 free used); 65 items for follow-up

items.requirement: Switches each of the 20 ports from 0.8 V (V55) to 8.4 V. The TPS259474LRPWR takes VIN only from 2.7 V. Answered under Raised by P1: V282: From 0.8 V the switch turns on and carries the port's current. The 3.0 A and the 570 mV this question names apply from 5.0 V up; below 5.0 V the drop is a reported figure, not a requirement (owner, 2026-10-01) V302: Yes. The search covers topologies that split the function across parts: a load switch from 0.5 V with separate reverse blocking, current limit and 20 V protection (owner, 2026-10-02)
items.reason: requirement changed after round 1 or round 1 left the function without a part (Research.md, Round 2, Follow-ups)

items.requirement: The continuous current one TPS55285 with its heatsink holds at 6.0 V in and 50 °C ambient, in A. This is each rail's continuous rating (owner, 2026-09-30). The heatsink's size is round 3's. Answered under Raised by P1: V279: 72.0 °C beside a servo converter and 66.25 °C beside the adjustable supply's converter: the junction stays at 125 °C or below at the 8 A typical inductor clamp. At 50 °C ambient without a heatsink a rail then holds about 2.47 A at 8.4 V from 6.0 V before it trips (owner, 2026-10-02) V281: 33 °C/W, the datasheet's RθJA on TI's 4-layer 2 oz EVM (SLVSI72A 5.3). The heatsink adds margin, which round 3 sizes (owner, 2026-10-01) V283: The rail's own latch: only that converter switches off, and it stays off until the operator clear control (F11) clears it. The other rails and the ESC keep running, and the firmware reports the trip (owner, 2026-10-01) V303: A latch part a research run selects, 4 a board; R3's 74LVC1G175GW,125 is the first candidate, SN74LVC1G74DCUR beside it (owner, 2026-10-02)
items.reason: requirement changed after round 1 or round 1 left the function without a part (Research.md, Round 2, Follow-ups)

items.requirement: Cuts the port off above 6.0 V (LV) or 8.7 V (HV), set by a jumper (F16). No candidate passed round 1: each failed the ±0.99 % HV trip band (V128) or the latch (V130). Answered under Raised by P1: V130: The port reconnects by itself once the rail falls below the ceiling, with the comparator's own hysteresis. No latch. The firmware reports the cut-off (owner, 2026-10-02)

items.requirement: CD4082, a dual 4-input AND gate, 3 a board (owner, 2026-09-30): its part number, stock and speed at 3.3 V. Answered under Raised by P1: V286: 3.3 V for the shift registers and the CD4082 gates; every alert node pulls up to 3.3 V (owner, 2026-10-01) V305: 74VHC21FT, a dual 4-input AND gate with stated figures at 3.3 V, in place of the CD4082; SN74LV21APWR beside it (owner, 2026-10-02)
items.reason: requirement changed after round 1 or round 1 left the function without a part (Research.md, Round 2, Follow-ups)

items.requirement: The alert thresholds, whether the monitors latch their alert outputs, and the critical line's blanking time, against the port switch's 3.96 to 4.84 A breaker and the INA3221's conversion time. The INA228 stays fixed (owner, 2026-09-30). Answered under Raised by P1: V288: Every temperature the board reads: the onboard shunt's sensor, the motor's thermocouple and infrared channels and the ESC telemetry's temperature, each with its own operator-set limit on the LIMITS page. Two consecutive conversions above the limit trip it. The ESC pack switch opens within the 500 ms stop deadline (V1) (owner, 2026-10-01) V304: Yes. The unmet stock gate is a current limitation, given to T6 as a stock exception, and the stock is read again before the order (owner, 2026-10-02)
items.reason: requirement changed after round 1 or round 1 left the function without a part (Research.md, Round 2, Follow-ups)

items.function: Servo supply; Servo supply temperature latch (new)
items.requirement: FU-2B2's P3 named the Servo supply temperature latch: it holds a rail off after its MCP9808 trips until the operator clear control (F11) clears it, 4 a board (V283). P2 returned no entry and no part was qualified. A latch part, R3's 74LVC1G175GW,125 first and SN74LVC1G74DCUR beside it (V303, owner, 2026-10-02). The Servo supply's requirement list carries V111's efficiency from the pack and the adjustable supply's 0.5 A floor and 50 mA step, which FU-2B2's list left out (adjudicator ruling 013). The pack's floor is 3.3 V a cell under load (V294); the converters stay checked from 6.0 V
items.source: V283, V303, V111, V294; FU-2B2, R6 P3 missed_functions and adjudicator ruling 013
items.reason: FU-2B2 left the function without a verified part (owner's rulings of 2026-10-02 under Raised by P1)

items.function: Port voltage ceiling; Port voltage ceiling latch

function the row names that P2 did not return: V126 requires the port switch to block current from the pin back into the rail (pin up to 12 V, switch on and off), and V302 (owner, 2026-10-02) names 'separate reverse blocking' as a part of the split topology. P2's rank 1 for Port supply switch, TLP3545A(TP1,F, takes this from the companion CMS04(TE12L,Q,M) (jlcparts C603062: 30 V, 5 A, 370 mV at 5 A, reverse leakage 8 mA at 30 V; the leakage at 8.4 V against V125's 5 mA is not read), and P2 states that selection.json holds one part a function and that the companions need functions of their own. P2 returned no entry for it: it carries its Schottky candidates (FSV1045V, SDT10A45P5-13, SS10P4-M3/86A) as drops under Port supply switch, so no part for it can reach selection.json.

function the row names that P2 did not return: V123 requires each port switch to limit its own current with the whole tolerance band between 3.0 and 6.35 A, and V302 names 'current limit' as a separate part of the split topology. P2's rank 1 takes it from the companion INA301A1IDGKR, which P2 says needs a function of its own because selection.json holds one part a function. P2 returned no entry and no requirements for it (limit band, trip against the 5 ms opening limit, 20 per board against a gate of 500, the alert's action on the photorelay LED), so the companion is unqualified in selection.json.

found_values.value: The INA228 of the cabled shunt path fills BENCH page 0x20 registers 0 (voltage) and 1 (current) whenever it answers; the ESC telemetry fills them only when no monitor answers. The two shunt paths replace each other (a test is cabled through one, never both), so one INA228 answers per test. How the firmware tells which path is cabled is not stated. Applied to Motor monitor as 'reading of record'

Yes: each INA3221's critical-alert output carries the 3.0 A ceiling to the main coprocessor on a shared line, its warning-alert output the 1.0 A stall threshold (owner, 2026-09-30); the firmware check at every sample stays on the measurement coprocessor

No rail monitor: one channel per port (owner, 2026-09-25) supersedes docs/Manifest.md:28's INA745A on the servo rail, as IOBoard.md's Conflicts in the tree records; the rail current is the sum of the port channels. The function takes no part

VBUS from the external shunt's pack-side sense lead, tapped ahead of the IN+ series resistor; the voltage is measured at the pack. The INA228's VBUS input is 0.8 to 1.2 MOhm, 0 to 85 V. Its protection is stage 2's (V306)
found_values.source: checkout bb10544e docs/Screens.md:131-134; hardware/docs/Research.md V306; INA228 SLYS021A 6.5 (ZVBUS, VVBUS)

found_values.value: 85 V from either lead to ground and 85 V between the leads, either polarity: a lead on the wrong terminal or the load side shorted puts the pack across them; R3 clamps the pack node under 85 V. The owner's answer to V306 sets the stage 2 protection to hold under 40 V between the leads, each input -0.3 to 85 V and 5 mA a pin through that fault
found_values.source: checkout bb10544e hardware/docs/IOBoard.md:464; hardware/docs/Research.md R3 row, F15, V306

found_values.value: 0 A to the positive full scale; every threshold in the servo code is positive

Thresholds: INA3221 critical 3.0 A = 30.00 mV on 10 mOhm, 750 counts of 40 uV, compared on each conversion; warning 1.0 A = 10.00 mV, 250 counts, compared on the averaged value (AVG 4). INA228 SOVL 30.00 mV, 24,000 counts of 1.25 uV (ADCRANGE 1) on both paths. Latching: INA3221 critical and warning transparent (CEN 0, WEN 0, the reset state), because the main coprocessor times the critical line against the blanking time and the warning line against 400 ms, and a latched output stays low until the measurement coprocessor reads Mask/Enable; INA228 ALERT latched (ALATCH 1), cleared by a DIAG_ALRT read at re-arm only. Blanking: 5 ms, one sample of the tree's 200 Hz sensor: longer than one INA3221 refresh (3 channels, shunt only, CT 100: 3.3 ms typ, 3.63 ms max), shorter than two (6.6 ms typ); the INA3221 states no minimum conversion time. Against the port breaker: the blanking acts on 3.0 to 3.96 A only; at 3.96 to 4.84 A the port switch's breaker acts
found_values.source: checkout bb10544e hardware/docs/IOBoard.md:113, :387, :389; docs/Servo.md:35-36; test/host/test_servo_limit.c:19; INA3221 SBOS576C 6.5 (tCONVERT), 7.3.2.1, 7.3.2.2, Table 8-34 (CEN, WEN reset 0h), https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ina3221.pdf; INA228 SLYS021A Table 7-16 (ALATCH, SLOWALERT), 7.6.1.13, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ina228.pdf

report.value: INA3221 critical 30.00 mV (3.0 A on 10 mOhm, 750 counts of 40 uV, each conversion); warning 10.00 mV (1.0 A, 250 counts, averaged value, AVG 4); INA228 SOVL 30.00 mV (24,000 counts of 1.25 uV, ADCRANGE 1) on both paths: 150 A x 200 uOhm and 300 A x 100 uOhm

INA3221 critical and warning transparent (CEN 0, WEN 0, the reset state): the main coprocessor times the lines (5 ms blanking, 400 ms stall) and cannot clear a latch, which only a Mask/Enable read on the measurement coprocessor's bus clears. INA228 ALERT latched (ALATCH 1), cleared by a DIAG_ALRT read at re-arm only; with ALATCH 1 any DIAG_ALRT read clears it, so the firmware must not poll DIAG_ALRT for CNVRF while armed

5 ms, one sample of the tree's 200 Hz current sensor. One INA3221 refresh (3 channels, shunt only, CT 100) is 3.3 ms typ, 3.63 ms max: a single conversion above 3.0 A holds its node low for at most 3.63 ms and is logged; two consecutive conversions hold it 6.6 ms typ and abort. The INA3221 states no minimum conversion time, so the shortest two-conversion pulse is not stated. Keep all 3 channels enabled on the 7th part so its refresh matches. Two parts' single trips that overlap on the shared line can exceed 5 ms together; the shift register names them

The critical threshold acts from 2.95 to 3.05 A (INA3221 26.2 mA plus ERJ-6CWDR010V 22.9 mA). The blanking covers 3.0 to 3.96 A only; at 3.96 to 4.84 A the port switch's breaker acts. The breaker band is the owner's figure (IOBoard.md:113, :389); R6's port supply switch has no part after FU-2B2 (selection.json), so the band rests on a switch not yet selected

INA3221 critical and warning limits reset to 7FF8h (positive full scale, alerts effectively off) and CEN, WEN 0; INA228 SOVL resets to 7FFFh and ALATCH to 0 (transparent). No alert carries an abort until the measurement coprocessor writes the limits, as IOBoard.md:113 requires before arming

INA3221 refresh 3.63 ms max a channel (shunt only, CT 100); port above 3.0 A to the first conversion wholly above at most 4.84 ms, plus 5 ms blanking: 9.84 ms plus the main coprocessor's action (V173). 7 parts on two buses, 4 and 3, 21 channels

INA228 averaged result every 8.42 ms (8.50 ms at -1 % oscillator) with AVG 4, 1052 us shunt and bus; ALERT within 17.0 ms of the crossing; shared ALERT line to a main coprocessor interrupt through the 74VHC21FT (cascade 27 ns max); the pack switch follows the enable node within the 500 ms stop deadline (V1, V288)
MCP9808T-E/MS two consecutive conversions: 500 ms at 0.0625 degC, 260 ms at 0.125, 130 ms at 0.25, 60 ms at 0.5 degC resolution; then the pack switch within the 500 ms stop deadline (V288)
The cabled path's INA228 whenever it answers; the ESC telemetry only when no monitor answers. How the firmware tells which path is cabled is not stated

Overcurrent 150 A onboard and 300 A external (V155), one averaged reading (V158); over-temperature: each temperature's operator-set limit on the LIMITS page, two consecutive conversions (V288); watched: the onboard shunt's sensor, the motor's thermocouple and infrared channels, the ESC telemetry's temperature

The delivered current is bounded by ILIM_AVG, 7 A min and 8 A typ with no maximum (SLVSI72A 5.4): at 6.0 V in, 4.57 A at 7 A and 5.15 A at 8 A (V111 loss model); 6.35 A at 8.4 V needs about 10 A of inductor current at 6.0 V and is reached at the 7 A minimum only from about 8.13 V in ((53.34 W + 3.59 W) / 7 A). found_values.value: The datasheet guarantees no efficiency. Typical figure derived from Figure 5-3 (VOUT 9 V, FPWM, TA 25 degC) read from the PDF's vector curves: converter loss fitted on the VIN 5 V boost curve, P = 0.2532 - 0.0973 IL + 0.0820 IL^2 W (IL 0.94 to 7.73 A); the same fit reproduces the VIN 9 V boost curves of Figures 5-5 and 5-7 within 0.13 W. 6.0 V in, 8.4 V out: 96.7 % at 1 A, 94.6 % at 3 A, 93.2 % at 3.72 A, 91.5 % at 4.57 A (IL 7 A), 90.2 % at 5.15 A (IL 8 A). 6.6 V in: 93.8 % at 4.12 A. Applied as 'Efficiency from the pack'

20 V steady, the top of the owner's 12 to 20 V DC input. The transient and its duration are not read: no page in the tree states them. The TPS55285 stops at VIN OVP 22.0 V min, 22.5 typ, 23.0 V max rising (0.9 V hysteresis); VIN is rated 27 V absolute maximum. Applied as 'Highest steady VIN'

The converters are checked from 6.0 V at the pack terminals (2 x 3.0 V, F9; Round 2 Follow-ups row: 'the converters stay checked from 6.0 V'). The board's pack floor is 3.3 V a cell under load, 6.6 V (V294, owner 2026-10-02), so 6.0 V is the conservative end. The drop across R5's pack path is not read here. Applied as 'Pack input range'
found_values.source: Research.md, Raised by P1 V294 (line 1007) and the FU-2G follow-up item for Servo supply; IOBoard.md:358 (checkout bb10544e89be)

found_values.value: 5.5 V and 8.4 V are nominal set points; the highest voltage at a port's supply pin is the F16 ceiling, 6.0 V (LV) and 8.7 V (HV). SLVSI72A gives VOUT_FULL 9.85 to 10.15 V on the 10 V range (VOUT_FS 01h, REF 0780h) and VREF 1.117 to 1.141 V at 1.129 V, 0.837 to 0.855 V at 0.846 V, 0.501 to 0.514 V at 0.508 V; with those, 5.5 V gives 5.40 to 5.59 V and 8.4 V gives 8.27 to 8.53 V (FU-2B2's derivation, which its P4 re-derived as 5.41 to 5.59 V and 8.27 to 8.53 V). Ripple and load-step overshoot depend on round 2's capacitors and are not included. Applied as 'Set point against the ceilings'

An output of the main coprocessor's I/O expander, with a pull-down that holds EN/UVLO below VEN_L 0.4 V while that output is an input (IOBoard.md Measurement coprocessor reset and Load gates at reset). A MODE resistor of 0 Ohm (75h) or 48.7 kOhm (74h) sets the default OE bit to 0 (Table 6-2). The rail's temperature latch (V283, V303) also holds EN/UVLO low: the two combine in an AND, whose part is not selected. Applied as 'Enable off at reset' and 'Temperature trip input'
found_values.source: IOBoard.md:115, :374 (checkout bb10544e89be); SLVSI72A 5.4 (VEN_L 0.4 V, VEN_H 1.03 V), 6.3.2 Table 6-2

found_values.value: 0 to 50 degC ambient, one range for the whole IO board (V7; V270). Applied as 'Ambient range' of every R6 function

found_values.value: 400 kHz (FSW 00b: 360, 400, 440 kHz). TI uses 400 kHz in its application and the inner current loop needs L above 1.2/fSW: 3.33 uH at the 360 kHz minimum. Applied as 'Switching frequency' and the inductor's 'Inductance'

Above 13 A, the peak inductor current limit at boost (ILIM_PK, typical, no min or max): an overload drives the inductor to it. Highest operating peaks with 4.7 uH less 20 % (3.76 uH) at 360 kHz: 9.33 A for the adjustable supply boosting 6.0 V to 15 V at the 8 A typical clamp (ripple 2.66 A); 8.63 A for a servo rail 6.0 V to 8.4 V at the clamp; 8.15 A for 20 V to 8.4 V at 6.35 A. Applied as 'Saturation current'

33 lines on the main coprocessor's I2C bus: 20 port switch enables, 5 bias selectors, 5 converter enables (4 TPS55285 and the TPS55288), the hardware latch read-back, and 2 inputs (DC input source status and brownout). GPA7 and GPB7 of the MCP23017 are output only and carry none of these, so 14 usable lines a part and 3 parts. The port supply switch topology of this run uses the same 20 enable lines (the INA301's RESET is tied to its port's enable) and adds none. Applied as 'Lines'

400 kHz: the only I2C rate in the tree is SET_I2C_KHZ, 100 to 400 kHz in 100 kHz steps, default 400. The TPS55285 takes 100 to 1000 kHz, the MCP23017 up to 1.7 MHz, the MCP9808 up to 400 kHz. Applied as 'I2C clock'
found_values.source: shared/settings/settings.c:105-107 (checkout bb10544e89be); SLVSI72A 5.5; MCP23017 DS20001952D; MCP9808 DS20005095B

found_values.value: Yes. The servo rail gate is R3's one high-side switch on each servo rail and on the adjustable supply's output, open within 5 ms of the enable node falling; the 20 port supply switches are driven through the I/O expander and are not the gate. Applied as 'Not the rail gate'
3.0 A continuous, the per-servo current ceiling at which the procedures abort at once; it applies from a rail of 5.0 V up (V282). Applied as 'Continuous current'

Yes: each port limits its own current, with its whole tolerance band between 3.0 A and 6.35 A: at or above 3.0 A the firmware abort acts first, and under 6.35 A, the rail's limit, one shorted port does not pull the other ports into the converter's limit. The specification names a port breaker of 3.96 to 4.84 A (IOBoard.md:113). Applied as 'Own current limit'

570 mV across the switch path at 3.0 A from a rail of 5.0 V up; below 5.0 V the drop is reported (V282). Basis: the LV setting's low edge 5.40 V (V114) against the lowest operating voltage of the low-voltage servo read, 4.8 V (Savox SH-0255MG+: 'Operating Voltage (V) 4.8V - 6.0V'), 0.60 V, less 30 mV in the 10 mOhm port shunt. Applied as 'Voltage drop'

Under 5 mA at 8.4 V: an open port leaks less than the idle current of the lightest load read, 5 mA ('Quiescent Current (mA) 5' for the SH-0255MG+ and the SB-2290SG); the same 5 mA placeholder as the servo rail gate (IOBoard.md:218). Applied as 'Off-state leakage'

Yes, with the pin up to 12 V, while the switch is on and while it is off: an ESC on a port drives its BEC onto the port's supply pin, and YGE's BEC 'is adjustable from 5.5V to 8.4V, with the Saphir series up to 12V'. Applied as 'Reverse blocking'

5 ms from an RP2354B reset to every port switch open: the specification's opening time for a power switch (servo rail gate, 5 ms from the enable node falling), inside V1's 500 ms stop deadline. Applied as 'Opening time after reset'

LV: may cut off from 5.59 V, must cut off by 6.00 V. HV: may cut off from 8.53 V, must cut off by 8.70 V. The lower edges are the highest set points of V114, the upper edges F16. The HV band is +/-0.99 % about 8.615 V, the LV band +/-3.5 % about 5.795 V. Ripple and overshoot are not included. Applied as 'LV trip band' and 'HV trip band'
found_values.source: F16 Answer (Research.md); IOBoard.md:386 (checkout bb10544e89be); V114 above

found_values.value: Not found: no source read gives a time a servo survives above its rating or a cut-off time for the ceiling. The Savox pages give operating ranges only (4.8 to 6.0 V, 6.0 to 8.4 V); docs/OpenYGE.md:253 states only that a BEC value above the servos' rating damages them. Recorded, not a pass or fail limit

8.4 V, 2 x 4.2 V a cell (IOBoard.md Pack voltage range, owner 2026-09-30). The SLS XTRON vendor page states no charge voltage, so 4.2 V a cell is not confirmed by the vendor. Applied as the top of 'Pack input range'

In boost the pack current is the inductor current: 5.59 A at 6.0 V at the 3.72 A continuous rating; in overload ILIM_AVG bounds it, 7 A min, 8 A typ, no maximum stated, so no maximum rules out a clamp above 9.9 A. Applied as 'Pack current at 6.0 V'

Peak inrush at most 2.35 A from the rail: the rail's 6.35 A setting less the 4.0 A a synchronised pair may draw on other ports (docs/Servo.md:68-69). The capacitance a port presents is not found: no servo or receiver page read gives one. Applied as 'Inrush'

6.35 A as the TPS55285 output current limit setting, enabled at reset, with OCP_DELAY 00b = 128 us at reset; hiccup off time 76 ms. It is a setting, not a bound: no tolerance is given at 6.35 A, and during the delay only ILIM_AVG (7 A min, 8 A typ, no max) bounds the output. The port's own limit (V123) acts first on one shorted port. Applied as 'Current into a shorted port'

Cut-off state: yes, read from the port monitor's bus-voltage reading, which falls behind an open switch; with V130 the firmware reports the cut-off. Jumper position: no; the setup screen lists the ceilings as set in hardware. Applied as 'Cut-off state readable'

20 V: the TPS55285 programs up to 15 V, its output OVP trips at 110.5 to 120 % of the set point, VOUT is rated 17 V absolute maximum, and a converter failed through passes the DC input, 20 V at most (V112). Applied as 'Input withstand'

Each of the 20 port switches switches its port from 0.8 V (V55) to 8.4 V; with V282 it turns on from 0.8 V and carries the port's current, the 3.0 A and 570 mV applying from 5.0 V up; with V302 the function may be split across parts (a switch from 0.5 V or below with separate reverse blocking, current limit and 20 V protection). TPS259474LRPWR takes VIN only from 2.7 V (SLVSFC9C 6.3, FU-2B2 reading 2026-10-02T14:00:46Z) and fails. A split topology passes: TLP3545A(TP1,F photorelay (C connection) + CMS04(TE12L,Q,M) Schottky + INA301A1IDGKR breaker. Applied as 'Operating input range' and 'Conducts from 0.8 V'
found_values.source: Research.md V277, V282, V302 (lines 990, 1015) and Round 2 Follow-ups row; IOBoard.md:384 (checkout bb10544e89be)

found_values.value: Each port is cut off above 6.0 V (LV) or 8.7 V (HV), set by a jumper (F16), with V128's bands; per V130 (owner, 2026-10-02) the port reconnects by itself once the rail falls below the ceiling, with the comparator's own hysteresis, no latch, and the firmware reports the cut-off. A cut-off below the band would cut a rail set from 0.8 V (V55), so the ceiling acts above the band only. Applied as 'LV trip band', 'HV trip band', 'No cut-off below the band' and 'Reconnect with the comparator's hysteresis'

data.ruling:
Both refutations hold, so the refutation stands.

1) Stock, sourcing rule 4. JLCPCB's exact LCSC match C2887910 is INA228AIDGSR, Texas Instruments, VSSOP-10. It has stockCount 0 and canPresaleNumber -236. Rule 4 fails a negative presale count whatever the stock says. The gate is 50 under S4 (5 x need, never under 50) and S7 (5 boards). That holds at 1 placement for this function (need 5) and at the part's 2 a board (need 10, IOBoard.md:465 'one INA228 for each path'). Stock 0 is under 50 either way. The part is not held: the Held parts table has no INA228 row, so rule 6 does not apply. The rule-5 second vendor fails too: Digi-Key reads 0 in tape and reel, cut tape and Digi-Reel, with a 20-week lead time.

2) Datasheet, series resistance. IOBoard.md:464 (owner, 2026-09-30) puts 1 kOhm in series with IN+ and with IN-. SLYS021A 8.1.4 and Figure 8-1 (RFILTER <100) say: 'Do not use values greater than 100 ohms for RFILTER. Doing so will degrade gain error and increase non-linearity.' 1 kOhm is 10 times that limit. Section 6.5 gives RDIFF as 92 kOhm typical only, with no minimum, maximum or drift. 2 x 1 kOhm in series reads about 92/94 = 0.979 of the true value, 2.1 % low (typical), and its drift has no bound. Research found +/-1 % for V166 (the owner's answer: for research), so 2.1 % misses it. V306 (owner, 2026-10-02) moves the TVS and the VBUS tap protection to stage 2 but keeps the 1 kOhm resistors. The conflict therefore stands against this function's own decided circuit.

The other checks pass and are not disputed. Lifecycle: Digi-Key Active, end_of_life false, discontinued false. Texas Instruments is on S1. The LCSC identity is correct. No part-level cause fails, which is why the scope is function. The stock gate is a quantity gate for this function's need, and the series-resistance failure is against this function's own requirement. This matches FU-2B2's ruling on the same function (016-adjudicator-R8-2.json).

The owner fixes the INA228 (Research.md Scope, Fixed inputs: Motor monitor INA228, owner 2026-09-30). V304 (owner, 2026-10-02) keeps INA228AIDGSR fixed despite the unmet stock gate. It treats that as a current limitation and a stock exception for T6, with stock read again before the order. A fixed input that fails a check is reported to the owner, not re-selected. So this ruling is a report to the owner, and the clash between the datasheet's 100-ohm limit and the owner's 1 kOhm is the owner's to resolve.

data.ruling: The refutation stands for the accuracy half of the figure. The noise half holds. servo_sim.c:22 sets noise_a 0.02f. servo_sim.c:44 returns (unit - 0.5) x noise_a, where unit runs from 0 to 1. That gives -10 to +10 mA, so 20 mA peak-to-peak. The +/-50 mA accuracy rests on "half the 0.1 A step of the absolute thresholds". No 0.1 A step exists in the cited sources or anywhere else in the checkout. servo_limit.c:59-61 sets knee_margin_a 0.15f, hard_limit_a 3.0f and stall_above_a 1.0f. servo_sync.c:36-37 sets min_depth_a 0.08f and hard_limit_a 4.0f. Servo.md:35-36 and :68 state these limits as 3.0 A, 1.0 A, 4.0 A, 0.15 A and 0.08 A. The settings schema holds no servo current threshold. The link pages carry current in 10 mA steps (link_pages.h:231, LINK_BN_CURRENT_CA). The 0.15 A and 0.08 A values are themselves off a 0.1 A grid, so a 0.1 A step contradicts the sources the claim cites. A one-decimal way of writing 3.0, 1.0 and 4.0 A is not a quantization step. It is also not a primary source for a measurement accuracy. The +/-50 mA is therefore the research's own choice, with a basis the sources do not hold. It was not found at a primary source, as P2 must record a value for research (V174 is "for research", owner, 2026-09-28). This is about the Port current monitor function's requirement value, not about any part. It does not refute INA3221AIRGVR or ERJ-6CWDR010V on any reading of their own figures.

data.ruling: The refutation stands, scope function. The specification line "External shunt class" (IOBoard.md:462, state "decided") limits the shunt to busbar type, 50 to 100 uOhm, 4.5 to 9 W at 300 A. The list instead gives a resistance of 50 to 136 uOhm, taken from P2's found value for V162. That found value takes its 50 uOhm floor from line 462 but replaces the same line's 100 uOhm ceiling with 40.96 mV / 300 A = 136.5 uOhm. The list also has no dissipation entry. A 136 uOhm part therefore passes the list while it dissipates (300 A)^2 x 136 uOhm = 12.24 W, above the decided 9 W. Research.md's Round 2 section says the specification holds where it differs, and a value found for research does not override a line the specification marks decided. So the list understates a decided requirement. The verifier's second point also holds as an omission. V165's row is filed under "R8, External shunt", and its found value of 25 mA or finer appears only under Motor monitor. With the 50 uOhm floor, the INA228 resolves 1.56 mA, so no part is wrongly admitted through that gap. The first point alone makes the refutation stand. The finding concerns this function's requirement list, not the selected part WSBE8518L1000JKA2: at 100 uOhm and 9 W it meets the decided class, though this ruling did not re-read its datasheet.
data.evidence: IOBoard.md:462 reads "External shunt class | busbar type, 50 to 100 µΩ, 4.5 to 9 W at 300 A. Part number: WSBE8518L1000JKA2 (R8) ... | decided; part: WSBE8518L1000JKA2, no second source (R8)". hardware/STATUS.md:50 gives the same class. Power.md's table under "Motor monitor (INA228)" gives 100 uOhm at 9 W and 50 uOhm at 4.5 W at 300 A. Research.md:875, row V162 (R8, External shunt), says "The pages give busbar type, 50 to 100 µΩ ... for research (owner, 2026-09-28)". Research.md:878, row V165 (R8, External shunt), is "for research (owner, 2026-09-28)". The found value for V162 in FU-2B2/003-P2-R8.json is "50 to 136 uOhm: lower bound the specification's busbar class (50 uOhm, IOBoard.md:462); upper bound 40.96 mV / 300 A = 136.5 uOhm". The claim under review repeats that range. For V165 the same file holds "25 mA or finer on the external path", which the claim's list does not carry. Arithmetic: 300^2 x 136e-6 = 12.24 W, against 9 W. Research.md's Round 2 section, line 538, says "this section and the specification hold".

data.function: re-rank drop: Port supply switch: VOM1271T or TLP3906(TPL,E with a discrete back-to-back MOSFET pair
data.ruling: The refutation does not stand, and the re-rank's drop holds. The driver facts hold at their sources. VOM1271T states only a typical toff of 65 us at CL 200 pF, with no maximum at any load. TLP3906 states toff 0.3 ms typical and 1 ms maximum at CL 1000 pF only, and its Fig. 12.8 curve against CL is for reference only. One point of the refutation is right: the re-rank's lower bound of 0.5 nF Ciss is wrong. Under rule 2, only two parts in jlcparts are allowlisted, 30 V, 19 to 30 mOhm at 10 V and stocked at 10,000 or more: Si4178DY-T1-GE3 (Vishay, Ciss 405 pF) and DMN3023L-7 (Diodes Incorporated, Ciss 873 pF). The refutation's 233 pF (C5148655, HXY MOSFET) and 20N03D (C19271463, HL) come from makers outside S1 and S2, so they are not candidates. That point does not carry the conclusion, because Ciss is the wrong measure of the driver's load. Ciss is a small-signal value at VDS 15 V. The TLP3906 must remove the gates' charge from its VOC (7 V minimum, 9 V typical) down to 0 V. The Si4178DY data sheet gives Qg 3.7 nC typical at VGS 4.5 V, and 7.5 nC typical, 12 nC maximum at VGS 10 V. That is about 0.75 nF per gate typical and 1.2 nF at the maximum. Interpolated to the 7 to 9 V of VOC, it is about 0.76 to 0.78 nF per gate, so 1.5 to 1.6 nF for the pair. Even with the whole Qgd of 1.3 nC left out, the pair is about 1.17 nF. Every figure is above the 1000 pF condition, the only one at which TLP3906's toff is guaranteed. The DMN3023L-7 pair is above it on Ciss alone, at 1.75 nF. No allowlisted stocked pair therefore puts the opening time inside a stated datasheet condition. VOM1271T has no maximum at any load. The drop's claim stands: the opening time after reset (5 ms, V127) is not stated at the load of a MOSFET pair, and no run selects the pair. Scope is function, because the ruling is about this function's opening-time requirement, not about either driver part.
